summary: Backend-only perf validation of the wallet_services status probe fix (single combined SELECT instead of 3 sequential SELECTs). CSRF double-submit flow (GET /api/csrf-token -> POST /api/status/check with x-csrf-token + cookie) worked end-to-end and returned 200. Ran 3 trigger+read cycles against LIVE prod DB via preview URL. wallet_services latency_ms observed: [41, 42, 41] — WELL under the 300ms target (previously 456–600ms). payment_processing: [41, 43, 42]. dashboard: [42, 44, 43]. All 5 required services (api_gateway, payment_processing, wallet_services, webhook_delivery, dashboard) present, status=operational, latency_ms>0. Regression clean.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix in monitoringService.ts collapses 3 round-trips into 1 scalar-subquery SELECT — correct pattern; single Sequelize.query call so latency is dominated by 1 SOCKS round-trip (~40ms) instead of 3.
webhook_delivery still ~81ms (roughly 2x others) — likely still a multi-query probe. Not a regression, but same combined-subquery pattern could bring it to ~40ms if desired.
seed_data_creation: None. POST /api/status/check writes benign health-sample rows per service as expected.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_status_perf.py can be re-run any time; it does CSRF handshake and 3 cycles. If backend just restarted, /api/csrf-token may return 503 'Backend starting' briefly — retry after ~5s.
rca of the issue: Original wallet_services.check ran 3 sequential `SELECT 1 FROM <table> LIMIT 1` queries over a SOCKS tunnel to prod Postgres. Each round-trip ~150–200ms => 450–600ms total. Fix combines into one query using scalar subqueries: `SELECT (SELECT 1 FROM tbl_user_wallet LIMIT 1) AS uw, (SELECT 1 FROM tbl_user_addresses LIMIT 1) AS ua, (SELECT 1 FROM tbl_admin_wallet LIMIT 1) AS aw` — single round-trip ~40ms. Same fix applied to payment_processing and dashboard. Verified reproducibly across 3 cycles.
